articleTitle: Modelling of the wind rotor of WECs for the analysis of wind effects influencing the drivetrain
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Improving the reliability of wind energy conversion systems is an important objective of research and of turbine construction. Especially oscillating loads at mechanical components induced through aerodynamics of the wind rotor cause additional expenses for maintenance. Real-time simulations of WECSs which include models of the wind rotor to simulate transients, facilitate the analysis of these oscillating loads and the development of advanced control algorithms for oscillation damping. Therefore, this paper presents a model of the wind rotor with adjustable accuracy and examines its influence on simulation results. Different wind effects that cause oscillating loads are analyzed using wind rotor models with varying accuracy. So limitations of model simplifications such as for real-time operation can be identified.

articleTitle: OPF integrating distribution systems flexibility for TSO real-time active power balance management
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Achieving reliably a high penetration rate of renewable energy sources (RES) in power systems requires tighter collaboration between the transmission system operator (TSO) and distribution system operators (DSOs) to exploit in a coordinated way the flexibility options (e.g. demand response, RES, etc.) available in active distribution systems (ADSs). To this end, the paper explores the integration to TSO operations of the flexibility options provided by DSOs at the TSO-DSO interfaces, focusing specifically on short-term (real-time) active power balance satisfaction. The flexibility at a TSO-DSO interface is roughly modeled, after aggregation by the DSO, as active/reactive power box constraints inside which the DSO constraints are met. The paper develops a tailored AC optimal power flow (OPF) problem, supporting the TSO to cover active power deficit at least cost by the adjustment of conventional generators and flexibility options from ADSs, while integrating flexibility constraints at TSO-DSOs interface besides classical constraints. The interest and effectiveness of the proposed approach are illustrated using the Nordic32 system.

articleTitle: Balancing services business use case development for TSO-DSO interoperability demonstration
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper introduces the emerging needs to strengthen the collaboration between transmission system operators (TSOs) and distribution system operators (DSOs) describing a methodology to investigate new TSO-DSO interactions. This methodology is based on Business Use Case (BUC) development, in accordance with standards IEC 62559 (Use case methodology) and IEC 62913-1 (Generic smart grids requirements). The proposed methodology is applied to the BUC “Activation of DSO-connected resources for balancing purposes in market environment” and the result is presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Thermal state analysis on bundled overhead line conductors
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Conductor position with respect to wind flow within bundle overhead line (OHL) system plays important role to determine its thermal state. At present, thermal state of bundled conductors are characterized by the heat transfer performance of single configured conductor or the upstream conductor which is fundamentally suitable for “low” temperature operation. However, for High-Temperature Low-Sag (HTLS) conductors that can operate at “high” temperature, this simplified characterization may not be sufficient due to high dissipated heat released from the upstream conductor to the nearby conductors located at the downstream position. COMSOL is used to further evaluate and provide initial insight on the thermal state of each conductors within bundle system. The results indicate that the use of simplified current-temperature relationship for bundled conductor (Joree, 47.75 mm) could overload the downstream conductor up to 4.5°C (2.25%) when is rated at I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">200°C</inf>. This signifies the needs to further evaluate the existing current-temperature calculation method for bundled HTLS conductors.

articleTitle: Comparing a simplified decentralized with an optimal centralized technique for after fault reconfiguration of radial distribution grids
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of reconfiguration of radial distribution grids is studied. Firstly, a decentralized reconfiguration method is developed, based on a simplified greedy algorithm that provides swiftly a feasible yet possibly suboptimal solution. The reconfiguration solution is calculated by using the information collected from the load flows before the fault and the line capacities. Next an optimal reconfiguration model is implemented based on an optimal power flow (OPF) setup, that integrates various network constraints. The two different methods are compared by testing different reconfiguration scenarios on IEEE distribution test feeders.

articleTitle: Optimal integration of distributed generators in the Iraq power system
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Iraq's power system is facing significant challenges due to the mismatch between generation and supply. According to some studies there is a need for around 6GW more capacity to meet the increasing demand. To overcome this problem a large number of households are using diesel generators, either private or shared installed at the neighborhood location. If the existing diesel generators are best placed could provide benefits to the grid by providing flexibility in localized areas and help to avoid or reduce the number of blackouts. This paper is proposing a methodology to find the best placement and the right size of the diesel generators in the Baghdad area. The optimization of these two parameters will reduce the real power losses, stabilize the grid voltage, and increase the network performance. This optimization approach will also contribute to minimizing the level of acoustical noise for existing diesel generators which they are installed at the neighborhood location. The objective function is looking to minimize the real power losses of the network and keeping the voltage within the permissible levels. The economic impact is also assessed by calculating the saving obtained when the diesel generators are best placed in the network.

articleTitle: Learning uncertainty of wind speed forecasting using a fuzzy multiplexer of Gaussian processes
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The smart power systems of the future will be able to accommodate wind power at a maximum efficiency by utilizing available information. For instance, information pertained to wind speed is essential in forecasting the overall amount of power generated by wind farms. Information is used to offset the inherent stochasticity of wind power and improve wind speed forecasting precision. In this work, an intelligent methodology for quantifying the uncertainty of wind speed pertained to forecasting is introduced. The introduced methodology adopts a set of Gaussian processes to assemble a model of the uncertainty of the forecasted speed. Results are taken on a set of real-world wind speed data.

articleTitle: Large signal stability analysis in clustering of microgrids using a hybrid method
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: By interconnecting microgrids (μgrids) it is possible to increase economic efficiency and security of supply. In order to analyse the transient stability (qualitative and quantitative) of power systems, a hybrid method can be employed, which comprises both time-domain analyses and energy function. The main goal of this paper is to study the transient stability of a cluster of off-grid μgrids comprising diesel generators using the hybrid method. For an operating point several short-circuit calculations were performed in the investigated grid. By using an energy function the results of the time-domain simulations were analysed in detail. Further, corresponding time and energy values, stability margin and critical clearing time (CCT) were determined. It can be concluded that, the deviations in the calculated CCT compared to the time-domain simulations for the considered three faults lie between 9 – 29 %.

articleTitle: Finite element modelling of Aeolian vibrations on stranded high-voltage OHL conductors
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The problem of Aeolian vibrations has been studied in indoor test-spans for many years. Its relevant standard experimentations have resulted in introducing the Energy Balance Method (EBM) which is the most commonly implemented method in the industry. Besides conductor properties, aerodynamic forces (Lift and Drag forces) acting on the conductor are the main input data for the EBM. The existing models frequently use experimental data of Lift and Drag forces for a cylinder. To further investigate the capabilities of wind-conductor interaction numerical modelling, it is useful to take advantage of Finite Element Modelling techniques. This paper simulates the wind flow around single OHL conductors with different outer layer stranding shapes and sizes utilizing COMSOL Multiphysics software. The simulations are based on solving the Navier-Stokes equation to compute the aerodynamic forces by integration of the pressure and shear forces within the boundaries of the conductor geometry. The numerical model computes the aerodynamic forces for three conductor geometries including smooth-surface, round-stranded, and trapezoidal stranding shapes. The numerically obtained solutions show that less aerodynamic forces are experienced by rounds and trapezoids compared to the cylinder geometry. This observation is true for high Reynolds numbers.

articleTitle: Distribution network planning using detailed flexibility models for DER
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The inclusion of new energy management technologies in buildings and increasing integration of distributed energy resources in electricity networks will require new operation and planning approaches from system operators. Currently, distribution network planning is rather inefficient as network assets are oversized to meet the peak demand of a worst case scenario which is unlikely to occur. In addition, flexibility provided by controllable loads is not taken into account at all. This paper presents an innovative approach that integrates the potential flexibility of distributed energy resources in the planning exercise. It incorporates two optimization problems: a low-level one to optimize the operation of controllable resources; and a high-level one based on an OPF that uses the available flexibility to solve network problems. The proposed method allows obtaining cost-effective solutions that make a better use of the flexible resources available, avoiding high capital investments in network reinforcement.

articleTitle: Reactive optimal power flow in the temperature-dependent power flow using interior point method with artificial neural network
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes the ANN-PDIPM-T method that apply the primal-dual interior point and artificial neural network simultaneously to optimize the losses in the temperature-dependent power flow. The temperature-dependent power flow (TDPF) considers the temperature in the branch of the electrical system, as the result of increased losses. To optimize the losses of TDPF, the methodology considered the primal-dual interior point method to power flow with a new variable, the temperature. In this case, the state variables are voltage, angle and temperature. The optimization process starts with the values of voltage and angle from Newton-Raphson Method and with initial temperature, as ambient temperature, in all branches. The neural network algorithm is incorporated to the interior point method with the aim to reduce of the computational complexity due to the insertion of temperature as variable. ANN-PDIPM-T method was applied to the IEEE-30, IEEE-118 and IEEE-300 bus system with reduction of the losses.

articleTitle: Robust optimization for the scheduling of isolated RES-based microgrids in developing countries
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: As of today, universal access to electricity is still a great challenge in developing countries, where grid extension is often a too expensive and time-consuming investment. Isolated systems are an effective solution to address the energy poverty issue. Hybrid microgrids, integrating conventional units and RES (Renewable Energy Sources) generators, are the most suitable option because they exploit resources which are locally available, clean, free and usually abundant. Both the planning and the operation phase are made particularly challenging by the intermittent nature of RES production and by the unpredictability of the demand behaviour and evolution in developing contexts. This work tackles this issue by developing a robust scheduling algorithm and providing a solution which guarantees the requested energy even in the worst possible condition, i.e. maximum demand and minimum RES production. A complete analysis of the reformulation procedure has been performed, in order to describe how to get a tractable counterpart by exploiting the strong duality theorem. The model has been applied to the case study of a missionary centre in Wau, South Sudan. It has been implemented in GAMS and the results have been compared with the output of the deterministic version of the algorithm.

articleTitle: On a method for testing ICA based blind source separation algorithm performance applicable in audio-based on-load tap changer diagnostics
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The biggest challenges in using Blind Source Separation (BSS) algorithms, such as those based on Independent Component Analysis (ICA), arise from the inability to determine the reliability of the resulting independent components (signals). In sensitive areas, such as machinery diagnostics, such uncertainties could also have a negative impact on decision-making processes. For that reason, any additional confirmation that yields a better understanding of BSS algorithm capabilities and the issues that may arise from using this method in solving audio-based diagnostic problems is desirable. In this paper, the focus is placed on On Load Tap Changer (OLTC) audio-based diagnostics. The dominant audio signals that mix with the carrier of the useful diagnostic material, in this case, express stationary character. Given the fact that the targeted OLTC audio fingerprint usually represents a highly non-stationary signal that appears only in a certain period when compared to these interferences, it is possible to develop a source separation method based on a simple modeling approach. For that purpose, in this paper, a non-linear latest square curve fitting method was used for the extraction of the OLTC audio fingerprint, which was then used as a reference for testing the source separation efficiency of several different ICA algorithms.

articleTitle: Bi-level minimum loading unit commitment for small isolated power systems
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The load demand of many non-interconnected island (NII) power systems exhibits high seasonal variability owing to the increased demand during the touristic summer season, against the low demand during the remaining year. The base load generating units of island systems are usually cheap, yet inflexible heavy fuel oil fired generators with large installed capacity and high technical minimum loading (TML) levels (in many cases up to 60% of the installed capacity). The higher TML of low-cost units renders them inflexible, particularly in low demand hours, where in some cases is necessary to dispatch flexible but costly peaking units (e.g. gas turbines), in order for the technical and security constraints of the unit commitment and economic dispatch (UC-ED) problem to be satisfied. This paper proposes a new UC ED method, solely based on the Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) approach, incorporating a bi-level TML technique for the conventional units of isolated island power systems aiming at avoiding the commitment of costly generation during low demand days. The methodology is applied to two indicative study-case islands and the obtained results are analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: Capacitances versus losses in medium-voltage transformer using bio-inspired computing
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis between capacitances and losses of medium-voltage transformer designs using artificial neural network. The equations of the capacitances include constructive parameters of the transformer, usually not available. This paper aims to calculate the capacitances using power rating, core losses concerning the magnetic flux density and load losses data of 1,936 transformer designs. The power ratings considered in this study were 30, 45, 75 and 112.5 kVA. The correlation between the data was executed by the artificial neural network using the Bayesian and Levenberg-Marquardt training algorithm.

articleTitle: Testing IEC 60870-5-104 and C37.118 based control center applications using a real time simulation platform
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The purpose of the paper is to develop a smart grid testing platform for the simulation of a large-scale power system using communication standards 60870–104 and C37.118 for analyzing real time control center applications. This testing platform comprises of the real time simulator developed by OPAL RT and specific monitoring software WinPP104 and PMU Connection Tester for imitating a remote grid control center. This investigation is carried out in the context of the Dyna Grid Control Centre (DGCC) project. The performance of the testing platform has been evaluated by integrating power system models developed in Hypersim, with soft PMUs and virtual RTUs for frequency monitoring and tele control applications. To suggest future development of the testing platform, suggestions for considering cyber physical vulnerabilities of the Operating Technologies (OT) and communication standards have been given.

articleTitle: Stability assessment of complex power systems — time domain simulations vs direct methods
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Due to the evolution of power grids into more complex, distributed and interactive systems the determination of stability under variable operating conditions has become more challenging. Stability analysis based on direct methods is a potential approach to assess the instabilities of complex power systems. Computer program-based analysis of computationally efficient and fast converging algorithms under variable and complex operating conditions is discussed in this paper. These computation algorithms determine system's stability along-with the bounds of all possible trajectories. Contrary to the classical stability assessment where time consuming simulations could impact transient performance, this approach is based on pre-disturbance system dynamics and determining stable and unstable equilibrium points with attraction regions.

articleTitle: Smart transformer control strategies for multi-microgrid islanding operation
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: In a framework with an increased number of small-scale generators connected to the distribution grid by inverters, the replacement of the electromagnetic transformers by Smart Transformers (ST) in secondary substations brings new opportunities to improve the grid flexibility. In this research, they are exploited in the context of Multi-Microgrids (MMG) allowing their operation in islanding mode, through the development of control functionalities to be incorporated in the converters of ST. The possibility to connect a storage device in the DC link, provided by a three-stage configuration (AC/DC/AC), fully decouples the control possibilities between Medium Voltage (MV) and Low Voltages (LV) grid sides. Even though energy storage cannot be considered, the frequency control of the LV grid can be also decoupled from the MV grid. In order to illustrate these set of possible approaches, two different configurations are addressed in the paper and their control strategies properly described: 1) with storage — the ST operates as grid-forming for both sides; 2) without storage — the ST just operating as a grid-forming unit for the LV side.

articleTitle: The impact of wind generator on Albanian power system transient stability
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Penetration of a large number of wind turbines into existing electric power systems can bring complexities in system stability, reliability evaluation and power management. This can lead to potential system problems during various disturbances. Transmission system operators should analyze the impact to the system parameters, and problems related to ancillary services and system stability. Analyses show the factors which affecting transient stability. The influence of the variations of rotary inertia on critical clearing time of power system transient stability is analyzed by time-domain simulation. We have study the impact of wind power plant on Albanian Power System transient stability. Simulations show that by replacing synchronous generators with wind power unit, the overall system inertia is decreased which lead to reduction of critical clearing time value. The difference between the critical clearing time in some cases is reduced up to 15% of the base case value.

articleTitle: Control developments in power electronics-based distributed generators for future grid services
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper presents practical experiences in an inverter-based microgrid installed at SEPIC research laboratory (Technical University of Catalonia, Spain). These experiences validate recent developments in the control of power electronics-based distributed generators which confirm the opportunity to provide auxiliary services for the utility grid. Harmonic rejection, voltage imbalance reduction, fault-ride through capability, and voltage and frequency regulation are some of the auxiliary services designed to improve the power quality of the future grid.

articleTitle: Model for defining the potential and value of multi-energy microgrid services to the low carbon power system operation
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Multi-energy system and more specifically, multi-energy microgrids (MEM) are expected to have a significant role in the future, low-carbon power systems. Their ability to provide both services to its customers and to the upstream system by means of local integration of distributed energy resources, provision of aggregation and energy storage services is very valuable. In this paper a bi-level approach to modelling is presented to inspect the behaviour of multi-energy microgrid that are interconnected with the upstream system through the exchange of prices signals. The MEM is defined as a market participant that can trade the energy. The energy trading and settlement is done in the upper level of the model where the energy prices are defined. In the lower level of the problem the MEM daily optimal scheduling of resources is done considering the dependent decision of the connection to the upper level. With the usage of duality theorem, the bi-level problem is converted into the single level problem that can be solved with available solver. The proposed model has been demonstrated on the simple illustrative example and the numerical results obtained show the validity of such approach.

articleTitle: The forecast of electricity consumption using SARMA model: Bosnia and Herzegovina case study
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper analyses the load forecast for a balance group using seasonal autoregressive moving average method. We investigate the importance of a precise load forecast under market conditions incorporating interests of different market participants. The seasonal autoregressive moving average method has been applied on total consumption of JP Elektroprivreda of Bosnia and Herzegovina d.d. — Sarajevo, with the purpose of the load forecast in three days ahead. Analysis results are presented for the data representing aggregated consumption of the balance group obtained from Independent System Operator in B&H, for the period from May 2016 to January 2018.

articleTitle: Optimal allocation of multiple unified power flow controllers using particle swarm optimization
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a new methodology to find the optimal locations and parameter settings of multiple unified power flow controllers (UPFC), using particle swarm optimization (PSO) in combination with a modified power flow method. The objective function aims at minimizing the generation cost of the network's generators ensuring the maximum possible profit for the electric power producer. The solution methodology consists of two phases. First, a new and simple way to model the UPFC is proposed. This model allows for the easy determination of the optimal settings for all UPFCs given their location and requires very small modifications to the standard optimal power flow algorithms. This new UPFC representation is combined with the standard PSO to determine the optimal location of each UPFC. The efficiency and accuracy of the proposed methodology is tested on a 39 bus power system and a 118 bus power system by comparing its results with those of the exhaustive search.

articleTitle: Unbalance and distortion evaluation in three-phase systems under non-stationary conditions
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a methodology to evaluate the unbalance and distortion presented in three-phase electrical power systems under non-sinusoidal and non-stationary conditions, using wavelet packet transform. Results on test systems and disturbances simulated by Matlab/Simulink demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Day-ahead management of smart homes considering uncertainty and grid flexibilities
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper presents an optimization model for Home Energy Management Systems from an aggregator's standpoint. The aggregator manages a set of resources such as PV, electrochemical batteries and Thermal Energy Storage by means of Electric Water Heaters. The resources are managed in order to participate in the day-ahead energy market, considering also local flexibility needs. The resulting model is a mixed-integer linear programming problem in which the aim is to minimize day-ahead operation costs for the aggregator while complying with DSO flexibility constraints in the form of maximum allowed net power exchange and ramping limits. Three sources of uncertainty are considered: day-ahead energy prices, PV production and load. Kernel Density Estimator and a backward reduction algorithm are used to create price scenarios and Robust Optimization is used to model PV and load uncertainties. The obtained results show the changes in the operation of the aggregator when grid flexibilities are considered and the impacts on the operation costs. In addition, a proposal for bidding in local flexibility markets is shown.

articleTitle: Improved real time emulator of a wind turbine dynamic model
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Design of an improved real time Emulator of a Wind Turbine Dynamic Model (EWTDM), based on an asynchronous motor driven by a frequency converter, is presented in this paper. The EWTDM emulates both the dynamic response and static speed-torque characteristics of a horizontal axis wind turbine model. In order to achieve a more precise emulation of the realistic situation, a torque reference of the frequency converter is compensated for viscous friction of the asynchronous motor and the difference between moments of inertia of the wind turbine and the asynchronous motor. An estimated value of electromagnetic torque of asynchronous motor is used as feedback signal to an additional torque PI controller. A desired speed-power characteristics of the load of the wind turbine is achieved by using a controllable load realized by a permanent magnet synchronous generator connected to a diode rectifier and DC/DC buck converter.

articleTitle: Preliminary viability assessment of an above-ground compressed air energy storage plant integrated in an existing wind farm
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper preliminary analyses the economic viability of an above-ground compressed air energy storage (CAES) unit integrated in an existing wind farm by means of calculating the maximum net present value and the maximum internal rate of return. For this reason, an optimization model is proposed in which the aggregate Wind-CAES plant participates simultaneously in the day-ahead energy market and in the frequency restoration reserve market of the Iberian system. Results of this study show that the CAES plant might be profitable only if the aggregate Wind-CAES plant participates not only in the day-ahead energy market but also in the frequency restoration reserve market of the Iberian system.

articleTitle: Disturbance accommodation control of wind turbines based on sliding mode approach
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a novel robust sliding mode controller design for wind turbines based on output feedback and disturbance rejection schemes. Considered horizontal axis wind turbine has 5MW capacity with variable speed. For this purpose, first, using rotor speed, system states are estimated while wind is considered as an exogenous state. Then, robust disturbance accommodation controller (DAC) based on sliding mode (SM) is developed. Finally, the efficiency of the proposed DAC-SM approach is compared with existing DAC method. As the results verify, DAC-SM scheme provides satisfactory performance against uncertainties.

articleTitle: Efficient regulation — precondition for electricity market development
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: A well-defined energy policy is a precondition for the successful development of any country. The European Union set the general objectives of national regulatory authorities. National regulatory authorities fulfill significant tasks in the Member States with respect to the creation of a fully operational internal market in electricity. Social regulation, Rate-of-return and RPI-X regulation are described in the paper. Special attention is paid to the mathematical basis of the RPI-X regulation and the weighted average cost of capital, which regulatory authorities use to ensure that returns are equal to the opportunity cost of capital.

articleTitle: Optimal sizing and economic operation of hybrid PV system for MBTS using meta-heuristic techniques
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to minimize the total lifetime cost of hybrid PV-diesel-battery system for mobile base transceiver station (MBTS), including optimal economic operation in addition to optimal sizing. This is performed using two different meta-heuristic techniques, namely genetic algorithm (GA) and crow-search algorithm (CSA). Both techniques and their optimization performance are compared. Solutions are tested by the dynamic and operation simulators respectively to check the system stability. Operation and maintenance (O&M) cost are calculated, as well as battery replacement costs associated to charging and discharging cycles and depth of discharge.

articleTitle: Incipient equipment failure assessment and avoidance through robust detection technqiue
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Key contributor to normal power grid operations is optimal working of the various power grid equipment/apparatus. Non-optimal operation of any of this equipment causes power quality problems which can pose great risk to the stability of the grid. Damaged or partially damaged equipment leaves characteristic signatures in the form of current and voltage waveform distortions. Detecting and localizing such signal distortions would contribute to grid reliability as the damaged equipment could be replaced in time before it can cause further damage. This paper proposes a Distortion Detection Technique (DDT) based on second-difference approach. This distortion detection technique has very low memory requirements and can be easily implemented on decentralized systems. The paper investigates the performance of this technique and evaluates it with case studies involving different kind of equipment failures simulated on Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS).

articleTitle: Accuracy performance of power voltage transformers
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Power Voltage Transformers, a novel concept in power systems worldwide, are units that incorporate features of both power and instrument transformers. Their primary purpose is power delivery. However, as they are still mainly specified according to standards for instrument transformers, their users sometimes expect simultaneous accuracy performance inherent to conventional voltage transformers. Due to a very large disproportion between the rated value of the burden on the power winding and the burden on the metering winding, achieving required accuracy classes is, at the very least, challenging both from design and testing perspective, and sometimes even impossible. The idea of this paper is to aggregate extensive experience the authors have with the topic of accuracy performance of Power Voltage Transformer units and provide examples, guidelines and recommendations on how accuracy performance should be incorporated into upcoming dedicated Power Voltage Transformer standards, and engineering practice. All conclusions and observations within this paper will be corroborated with the results of measurements performed on actual units, calculations or both.

articleTitle: Analysis of the wind generation impact on inertial and primary frequency response of the Croatian electric power system
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This research examines the impact of wind penetration in the Croatian power systems on system frequency stability. The main focus of the research is the simulation of system frequency response on the mathematical model of Croatian power system. With these models the possibility of providing wind inertial response and primary frequency response will be examined. Characteristics of frequency response such as the value of frequency nadir, the steady-state frequency deviation and the rate of change of frequency will be compared for all investigated cases. This paper uses low-order system frequency response models to simulate power system frequency changes. Also, most of the block parameters are provided and are accurately calibrated to model “real life” processes. The models are developed and implemented in the MATLAB/Simulink and tested on “real life” case in Croatian power system.

articleTitle: Self-inductance variations in dynamic inductive charging of EVs
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Dynamic inductive charging can effectively address concerns linked with the Electric Vehicles' limited travel range, allowing the vehicle to wirelessly receive energy, while moving on the road. Compensation capacitors, usually selected according to the self-inductance of the magnetic coupler's coils, are used in inductive charging in order to increase the transferred power and the system's efficiency. Although the variations in the values of the self-inductance are not significant while the EV moves over the station, they can considerably modify both the transferred power and the system's efficiency. This paper studies the variations in the output power and the system's efficiency due to the values of the coils' self-inductance in dynamic inductive charging of EVs, while also investigating the values of the compensation capacitors due to the aforementioned variations. A magnetic coupler is simulated in order to study the results of the presented analysis.

articleTitle: Multidimensional smart meter data analytics based on sparse representation technique
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Customer's electricity consumption data analysis is very helpful for distribution system operators and electricity retailers in many aspects such as demand response and load forecasting. Dictionary learning and sparse representation techniques can extract important features of a load curve, which has not been properly applied in the current literature. In this paper, a sparse representation-based multidimensional framework for analyzing user behaviors is proposed from the aspects of behavior modeling, variability modeling, and preference modeling. Concretely, behavior modeling includes basic characteristic analysis, spectrum-based periodic pattern analysis, and working/off day pattern analysis. Variability is modeled through entropy analysis of user patterns. Finally, customer's preferences are modeled from the distribution of partial usage patterns. Numerical experiments prove the effectiveness of the analysis.

articleTitle: Evolutionary load morphing in smart power system partitions ensuring privacy and minimizing cost
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The Smart power refers to adaptation of information technologies in power system applications. Information utilization accommodates the development of new capabilities in effective power systems management. In this paper, a new methodology is presented for load morphing at a nodal level. In particular, the methodology is applied to cases where multiple consumers are connected to a local area grid and they can collectively manage their consumption. The goal is to morph their group consumption in such a way that shares two characteristics: (a) the consumption cost is low, and (b) the privacy of the consumers is retained. Modelling of the goals is performed via a multi-objective optimization problem whose solution is found with the use of an evolutionary algorithm and more specifically of the non-dominated sorting algorithm-II (NSGA II). Results exhibit the high potential of the methodology in morphing the load demand in such a way to ensure privacy and low cost of electricity consumptions.

articleTitle: Impact of cyber-security breach to price signals on power market: An experimental human simulation
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The market power is a term defined in power economics as a potential to make the electric power market volatile. A supplier having the market power has an opportunity to speculate on the market clearing price. Observance of the market power may be destructive for the system only if a supplier actually exercises its potential. Although there are several studies on the assessment of market power, there is no study showing the consequences if a supplier stealthy exercises its market power. In order to fill this gap in the literature, a multi-player electric market game is developed and a realistic market environment is simulated with the participation of engineering students. Mainly the cyber-security issue in conjunction with the market power is focused in this study. For a limited number of periods, price information is intentionally corrupted via cyber-attack to create a misbelief at the supplier side. The analysis of the results showed that if a participant is under the impression of possessing the market power regardless actual possession, he/she would try to exercise it to raise its profit, and as a result, market clearing price starts to fluctuate.

articleTitle: Decentralized electricity trading in the microgrid: Implementation of decentralized peer-to-peer concept for electricity trading (P2PCET)
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Ongoing decentralization of electricity generation enables households to invest in small renewable energy sourced generation and to benefit from those investments by selling electricity and by selling their flexibility in demand and generation. Individual households including end consumers, producers and prosumers (acting as peers) could trade within community microgrids. The idea of decentralized electricity trading in a microgrid can be achieved with distributed ledger technology for peer-to-peer transactions. In this paper, this issue is examined and some ideas behind the concept discussed.

articleTitle: Conversion error of second order polynomial ZIP to exponential load model conversion
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper analyses the conversion error that occurs when second order polynomial (i.e. ZIP) load model is converted to exponential load model. Two conversion methods are used: an analytical method and a non-linear least squares based method. The conversion error of both methods is described and compared based on numerical analysis. It is shown that the load model conversion error depends on the input load model parameter values, used method, chosen voltage and the voltage sensitivity of the characteristic.

articleTitle: Strategic participation of merchant energy storage in joint energy-reserve and balancing markets
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Energy storage systems (ESS) may provide the required flexibility to cost-effectively integrate stochastic electricity generation from renewable energy sources. Energy storage owners should, however, be properly remunerated for the services they provide. In this paper, we propose a bilevel optimization problem, mimicking the strategic behavior of a price-making ESS owner in a joint day-ahead (DA) energy-reserve market. We explicitly consider possible real-time balancing market outcomes when clearing the DA markets via probabilistic reserve constraints and ensure the feasibility of dispatching ESS-based reserves through novel worst-case reserve activation constraints. The proposed framework may be used by regulators and market operators to assess market design options or by ESS owners to optimize their bids.

articleTitle: Future operational concepts for reactive power compensators in transmission grids
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: An increasing number of technologically diverse reactive power compensators in the transmission grid require more complex operational concepts. This paper presents a new method for the simulation of the reactive power dispatch, which consists of a 2-stage optimization model. In the first stage, an optimal reactive powerflow optimizes the reactive power dispatch iteratively for the considered period using successive linear programming with an embedded discretization process. The second stage determines the optimal switching times based on the grid losses of individually optimized time-coupled periods. For deriving reactive power schedules, the time intervals between switching operations as well as the utilization of certain reactive power compensators by a closed-loop are investigated. By investigating sensitivities, it becomes apparent that the automation of flexible devices like STATCOMs enables a reduction of switching actions for the remaining devices.

articleTitle: Short-term ampacity forecasting based on linear regression in a distribution line
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Generally, electric companies consider static thermal ratings for overhead lines, which are based on conservative weather assumptions. However, weather forecasts can be used for the operation of distribution lines to determine the ratings dynamically, some hours in advance. However, weather forecasts may be not accurate enough to operate the grid securely, so different statistical methods can be used to get closer to the actual conditions. This paper implements a statistical method to improve the security of ampacity prediction.

articleTitle: Expert system for topological remedial action discovery in smart grids
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: For power grid congestion management, lots of research have focused on using generation redispatching, load shedding or demand side management flexibilities. However, a less costly option would be grid topology reconfiguration. Branch switching has been previously explored, since it could be formulated as a linear programming optimization problem we can solve, and showed some benefits. This can further be extended to the broader class of non-linear nodal reconfigurations at substations. In this paper, we present an expert system to automatically discover such topological remedial actions on congested grid states. It comes with a new adapted grid representation, conditional to the congestions of interest, which can be interpreted by operators. To test our expert system, we independently run it on thousands of realistic congested French grid states from 2012 to 2014 with a remedial action discovery success rate of 75%. Our exploration is quite efficient, since it is limited to single substation topological action and is usually successful on first try, even in the case of overloads above 30%.

articleTitle: A unified model of peer to peer energy trade and electric vehicle charging using blockchains
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: In this paper we develop a trade model that integrates peer to peer energy trade with Electric Vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. As an energy distribution network may not allow energy transfer among microgrids, in the proposed trade model, each microgrid operates one local charging station and microgrids form coalitions to trade EV charging requests among themselves for the optimal utilisation of renewable energy. Our main contribution is a multifaceted marketplace using blockchain where prosumers, microgrids and EVs participate in energy trade. Using blockchains, we present distributed scalable computation methods for trade decisions which are robust against malicious and faulty participants.

articleTitle: Operation of a wind-PV-battery hybrid power station in an isolated island grid
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Hybrid power stations (HPSs) constitute virtual power plants comprising storage and RES facilities operated by a single entity, the HPS operator. The HPS concept applies in saturated insular power systems as a means to increase renewable penetration. The main objective of this paper is to investigate the operation of a small non-interconnected island (NII) power system incorporating a relatively large hybrid wind-PV-battery power station. The anticipated benefits for the system due to the HPS will be quantified in terms of system economics and renewables penetration, while indices related to the annual operation of the local power station comprising thermal units will be assessed as well. The exploitation of the available renewable energy of the HPS will be examined and the internal operation of HPS components will be evaluated. A MILP-based optimization generation scheduling approach will be used to perform daily and annual simulations.

articleTitle: A case study of residential electric service resiliency through renewable energy following Hurricane Maria
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Electrified societies require continuity of electric service to supply basic human needs. Hurricanes in the Caribbean present a significant challenge to the continuity of the electric service. In this paper we present a case study of residential system resiliency with the adaptation of an existing residential photovoltaic system in Puerto Rico, grid-tied under a net metering agreement with the utility, to a stand-alone system with batteries to provide continuity of service after Hurricane María. Then, we present and analyze recorded data of the electric demand behavior and essential loads behavior at the residence prior to Hurricane María, when the residence was connected to the functioning electric grid at full load, and after Hurricane Maria when the residence was operating disconnected from the electric grid with diminished electric demand. Furthermore, we perform an economic analysis between the PV system and an equivalent gasoline inverter generator. Our analysis serves as a feasibility study of the use of stand-alone photovoltaic systems to increase residential resiliency in Caribbean islands after a hurricane.

articleTitle: An experimental forensic testbed: Attack-based digital forensic analysis of WAMPAC applications
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The global trend is to go digital, in other words, go ‘smart’. Like the rest of the world, power sector is also getting smarter hence the term smart power grids and substations. Such capability comes at the price of heightened risk of potential cyber threats to substations. With all such potential risks, we must be able to trace back and attribute any potential threats to its root. In this paper, we're exploring substations to find potential evidence in case a forensic investigation becomes a necessity. Moreover, a forensic experimental testbed is proposed for digital forensic analysis. Finally, a mapping of attack-based forensic evidence is presented.

Author Keywords: Wide Area Monitoring Protection and Control

articleTitle: Distributed co-simulation for collaborative analysis of power system dynamic behavior
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Given the complexity, scale and heterogeneity of modern power systems, many comprehensive simulation tasks are almost impossible to carry out without collaboration from multiple institutions. One way to approach collaborative simulation is through co-simulation. In this approach each institution contributes a model and the simulation is run distributedly. Co-simulation environments can be centrally orchestrated or decentrally orchestrated, each having its own set of advantages and challenges. In this paper we analyse the merits and challenges of co-simulation for collaborative simulation between institutions through two simple co-simulation environments, one centralized and the other decentralized. We argue that a co-simulation environment for collaboration between institutions should provide functionality like standard co-simulation interfaces for a variety of simulation tools, remote management and configuration, model compatibility checks, and failure detection and recovery. An environment with these characteristics can be easily adopted by a wide range of institutions, which would greatly aid in tackling the complexity of modern electrical power systems.

articleTitle: Advanced metering applications in microgrids: A hardware-in-the-loop electric power setup
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Distributed generation including renewable energies have spurred the development of microgrids as a new alternative to electric energy system. We have built the Sustainability Energy Center (SEC) at the University of Puerto Rico Mayagüez (UPRM) and within it developed a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) setup that allows researchers, graduate and under graduate students and others to acquire a deeper understanding of microgrids, microgrid integration and control and renewable energy. In this paper we present the design and implementation of the HIL focusing in energy management system (EMS) and advance metering components. Experimental results of a demand response application using meter data is also developed and presented.

articleTitle: A hybrid agent-based secondary control for microgrids with increased fault-tolerance needs
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid secondary control architecture for microgrids with AC-coupled droop-controlled units, based on both centralised and distributed control principles. The proposed secondary control is based on a multi-agent system (MAS), complemented by a microgrid centralised controller (MGCC). The system is able to adjust the droop curves dynamically in order to achieve voltage/frequency restoration as well as active/reactive power optimal allocation, based on the actual status of the controllable units, in particular, the state-of-charge of batteries and maximum power point of photovoltaics. The distributed nature of the agents is also fully exploited because the proposed framework retains operability even under fault on secondary MGCC. To evaluate the proposed framework, a scenario-based performance analysis has been tested over a simulated AC islanded microgrid, where communication from the MGCC is suddenly interrupted and the MAS is required to reconfigure in order to maintain the same control objectives. MATLAB/Simulink simulations have been realised using detailed physical form models for a small-scale microgrid, while the implementation of the MGCC and MAS is accomplished through Java Agent Development (JADE) framework.

articleTitle: Vector surge and ROCOF protection algorithms for distributed generator islanding detection
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper presents the study of parameter and condition determination in proposed algorithms for vector surge and rate-of-change-of-frequency protection. Vector surge and ROCOF relays are the mainstream protection devices for anti-islanding protection of utility embedded synchronous generators. The protection settings parameters are determined with the use of practical formulas and grid proposed conditions. With the parameter and condition acknowledgement proposal for a new vector surge and ROCOF protection algorithm was written. Formulas presented in this paper are directly derived from the generator swing equation, given grid protection conditions and events.

articleTitle: SCADA maintenance and refurbishment with security issue in modern IT and OT environment
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: When working with SCADA systems, transmission system operator faces challenges, which arise from several issues that appeared over the last 10 years. SCADA system is a crucial application for power system control. Refurbishment of those systems are usually planned once in a decade or even rarer. This strategy is now undergoing a change because of intertwinement of SCADA systems with IT industries. Hardware platform for SCADA originates from IT world, which has different rate of technology change. With new IT landscapes, cyber security issues strongly influence the whole SCADA environment. Those facts and aspects will be presented in detail in this paper, with examples from real Transmission system operator (TSO) experience with in depth analyses of issues TSO faces in everyday operation.

articleTitle: Synergies between electric vehicles and distributed renewable generation?
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Prosumers represent an important building block under the paradigm of a decentralized energy landscape such as outlined in the EU Clean Energy Package. However, the synergetic use of distributed resources such as electric vehicles (EV) or residential roof-integrated photovoltaics (PV) on household or neighbourhood level requires their diffusion patterns being temporally and spatially synchronized. This paper is dedicated to the joint analysis of their adoption patterns, using spatial analysis interfaced with mutual information and criteria ranking analysis. Surprisingly, outcomes for Portugal suggest that residential photovoltaics and electric vehicles are adopted by different population layers, as their occurrence is linked to diverging sets of socio-demographic criteria. Furthermore, an analysis of these criteria sets shows that their internal composition (the driving factors behind EV and PV adoption) varies among regions which has important implications on electricity network planning.

articleTitle: A simple model to analyse the frequency behaviour of interconnected power systems with high renewable penetration
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This work presents a model for the simulation of frequency response after power imbalances. The model relies on the tuning of four parameters to adequately represent the frequency behaviour. The performance of the proposal is tested in the Synchronous Grid of Continental Europe. Probable future operation scenarios are developed from publicly available data. Then, several simulations are executed to assess the behaviour of the primary frequency control in low inertia scenarios.

articleTitle: Predictive voltage control for LV distribution grids exploiting flexibility from domestic customers
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: In order to avoid voltage problems derived from the connection of large amounts of renewable-based energy generation to distribution networks, new advanced tools need to be developed that are able to exploit the presence of Distributed Energy Resources (DER). This paper describes the approach proposed for a predictive voltage control algorithm to be used in LV distribution networks in order to make use of available flexibilities from domestic consumers via their Home Energy Management System (HEMS) and more traditional Distribution System Operator's (DSO's) resources, such as transformers with On-Load Tap Changer (OLTC) and storage devices. The proposed algorithm for the Low Voltage Control (LVC) is detailed in this paper. The algorithm was then tested through simulation using a representative Portuguese Low Voltage (LV) network in order to assess its performance in several future scenarios with different operating conditions. The future prospects for field-trial validation in a Portuguese smart grids pilot are also discussed.

articleTitle: Analysing frequency support from DFIG-based wind turbines — impact of parameters and initial conditions
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Enabling the type-III and type-IV wind turbine generators to participate in grid frequency control couples them to the electromechanical modes of the grid. In this paper we have investigated how initial wind speed, rotor-side controller parameters, PLL parameters and pitch angle controller parameters influence the virtual inertial response and primary frequency response of the total power controlled DFIG-based wind turbine generator. Preliminary analysis shows that although there is some influence of these parameters, most of them are not significant. However, further and more in depth research is needed. Furthermore, we discuss the results with respect to other research related to this topic.

articleTitle: Analysis of possibilities of alleviating repercussions caused by large disturbances in the power system
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Various EU regulations have established rules for accessing the electricity exchange grid in order to ensure proper functioning of the electricity market while maintaining a proper level of system security. System security depends on the technical capabilities of its components to withstand disturbances and to help prevent serious interruptions or to re-establish system operation after a breakdown occurs. This paper generally gives a theoretical and practical overview of measures for the automatized protection against voltage disruption and reduction of the active or reactive load of lines or transformers in the subsystem PrP Osijek. In addition to automatic protection, measures of excluding certain elements of the grid will be shown, as well as functions for blocking/activating the regulation of grid elements in order to reduce active and reactive loads of lines or transformers. The analysis gives the effect of some measurements on a real transmission grid model. The model had to be adjusted with the grid state and load requirements that anticipated various unfavourable scenarios, which could cause the power system to break down.

articleTitle: Building automation systems and smart meter integrated residential customer platform
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Building automation systems (BAS) have promising potential to support power and energy management applications, in addition to the current and conventional intention of use for improving comfort. Integration of BAS with smart meters to provide remote monitoring and control over user-friendly interfaces can foster consumer awareness, proactiveness towards more effective use of energy and it is one of the keystones of the future's smart cities. This paper proposes development and field implementation of a remote monitoring, control and data processing system for residential customers. The system is designed to comprise a widely used BAS protocol (KNX) and smart meters in the market, adding on a central database and a web application. The developed solution is implemented in 3 houses with real residents in Istanbul, Turkey. The study provides developments for hardware-software integration in building energy management and solutions for problems encountered during field implementation. Energy management potential of three houses from the field is also discussed.

articleTitle: Adaptive clustering method for LV customer profiling
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The evolution of power systems, especially at distribution level, is particularly fast due to many novelties, as the impressive growth of distributed energy resources based on renewables and the economic drivers towards “full-electric” energy consuming scenarios (i.e. electric vehicles, electric air conditioning, cooking appliances, etc.). There is a general consensus in Literature that time series of consumption and generation are necessary to properly represent the impact of demand coincidence and of generation-load homotheticity. Thus, accurate modelling of production and demand becomes crucial to make rational hypotheses for network development and management, both at MV and LV level. Worldwide TSOs and DSOs use typical daily profiles for representing the consumption of the end-users. Updating these typical load profiles to the new behavior of current customers is often disregarded, and the used profiles refer to out-of-date and limited measurement campaigns. This paper proposes a clustering method for finding updated typical load profiles for different category of customers (household, commercial, industrial), able to be adapted if any change in the electrical behavior of customers occurs. In the paper results obtained by applying the proposed methodology to a large database of real consumption profiles of end-users in Italy have been discussed.

articleTitle: PI and state space speed control for drive systems with elastic coupling and very small inertia ratio
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The speed control in many industrial applications is required to have high dynamic properties. In addition, for drive systems with an elastic coupling between the motor and load side, the damping of oscillations during operation is desired, in order to limit the stress on mechanical parts of the drive system and improve process quality. This paper aims to present and evaluate common tuning methods for PI and state space control structures in elastically coupled drive systems with a very small inertia ratio. The mathematical model of a two-inertia system is used to establish the controller design. For the PI control, the symmetric optimum and the pole placement method are considered. Better oscillation damping can be achieved with the state space control. It produces lower settling times by using all system states for control purposes. Here, an appropriate controller design is necessary to avoid excess levels of the required plant input. For both controller topologies, a simulation of the system disturbance reaction is used to evaluate their performance.

articleTitle: Prony analysis and Robust RLS for electromechanical oscillations: An evaluation technique
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: This paper investigates a combination of methods to extract modal information from synchrophasor measurements. Ringdown measurements have been preprocessed with Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), analyzed with Prony's method and the results postprocessed with clustering techniques. Ambient measurements before and after a disturbance have been analyzed with Robust Recursive Least Squares, with the same clustering technique applied for continuous evaluation of the estimated modes. Together, ambient and ringdown analysis provide accurate, near real-time awareness of electromechanical oscillations. Postprocessing logic is an issue for parametric methods, as higher model orders often are chosen to improve the estimation process. This paper demonstrates that close inspection of true and trivial modes can reveal important properties of the estimation, and that they can be used to evaluate if the choice of parametric model is justified for the analyzed signal.

articleTitle: Active damping of LCL filter resonance based on capacitor-current feedback in grid-connected VSC
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: In order to meet grid codes and to reduce cost, LCL filters are widely used in grid-connected converter applications such as in decentralized renewable energy. They provide a higher damping ratio and smaller components than L filters, but they also impose stability issues due to their inherent resonance. This paper deals with different damping approaches to overcome this drawback and discusses the capacitor-current feedback based method in detail. The impact of active damping gain on system stability and closed-loop current control is discussed and illustrated by simulation. Experimental results validate the presented approach.

articleTitle: Aggregated active and reactive power and energy management of distributed energy resources and performance evaluation
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Aggregated management of distributed energy resources (DERs) is an emerging topic mainly with simulation based investigation of the developed approaches. On the other hand, field tests can provide important insights on the path to wide deployment. Most of the works take into account aggregated DERs as a single entity and do not get into details about how to allocate a desired management target among them. This study focuses on management of different types of DERs as a group to reach aggregation targets through two field-testing scenarios. Active power management scenario investigates management of a DER group for an hour long period by allocating an overall target proportional to DERs energy storage capacities. Varying PV panel, wind turbine and residential consumer power profiles were also included in the testing scenario as a challenge to determine set points for manageable devices. Reactive power management case equally distributes aggregation targets among available DERs, comparing relative management performances in 4 consecutive periods. Management performances of individual DERs and the whole group were evaluated, highlighting management accuracy and possible challenges in the field.

articleTitle: Grid voltage regulation with optimal reactive power effort by active front end converters
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Facing the challenges of a predominant power generation by renewable energies such as decreased power quality and supply reliability issues, power systems grid-connected by active front end converters are increasingly required to provide grid supporting measures. This work deals with an advanced control strategy proposed to automatically stabilize the grid voltage within a permitted tolerance band while simultaneously keeping the provided reactive power at a minimum or optimum level. Simulation and experimental results validate the proposed voltage controller. A simulation-based case study is provided to demonstrate its control performance for multiple grid-connected active front end power converters.

articleTitle: Utilizing flexibility in microgrids using model predictive control
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: We derive a control strategy for the operation of Microgrids (MGs) with high shares of Renewable Energy Sources involving Model Predictive Control (MPC). By combining the MPC with an Energy Management System (EMS) utilizing stochastic programming techniques and a sufficiently large temporal optimization window we improve the point of operation of the system regarding both short and long-term operational aspects. We aim for a system operation that allows for the utilization of the MG as a Virtual Power Plant. In this work we focus on the predictive controller design and the incorporation of information derived in the EMS layer.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of wind turbine fast frequency response control on electrically distanced active power disturbance mitigation
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: In a power system, increased wind energy penetration changes the dynamic system response to active power disturbances. Due to the lack of natural inertial response from converter connected wind sources, an advanced converter control is required for maintaining a transient frequency stability of modern power systems with high shares of renewable energy sources. This research examines the new wind turbine fast frequency response control capability on the addressing electrically near and distanced active power imbalances considering transient dynamics system parameters. The focus of this research is to analyse the effectiveness of wind turbine fast frequency response control in reduced inertia power system modelled as a four-inertial centre system. The study is done on the case of Croatian power system with “real life” data for power generation, wind production, primary frequency regulation, and load shedding schemes. The simulation and scenario analysis are conducted under the MATLAB/Simulink environment using detailed power transmission system model.

articleTitle: Bottom-up approach to compute der flexibility in the transmission-distribution networks boundary
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: The integration of Renewable Energy Sources, mainly in distribution grids, has been changing the paradigm of power systems operation. This constitutes an opportunity to make use of flexible energy resources to support DSOs and TSOs on network operation activities. The amount of total flexibility available in the system can be quantified starting from lower voltage levels considering the implementation of demand response schemes. This work is focused on the development of an expeditious methodology to assess the total flexibility of low voltage consumers and aggregate it by means of a bottom-up approach until reaching the transmission network nodes.

articleTitle: Characteristics of residential battery storage system for better integration with electric distribution system
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: Our objective is to determine the characteristics of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), based on different battery technologies characteristics, which will best operate in parallel with an existing electric distribution grid, to fulfill the requirements of residential customer services. To achieve our goal a set of the more common battery technologies used nowadays is defined to combine their performance characteristics in one system. We present preliminary results using ES-Select software to select the battery technologies to combine.

articleTitle: Controlled islanding of power systems considering voltage stability constraints
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
abstract: An Intentional Controlled Islanding (ICI) algorithm that directly determines an islanding solution with minimal power-flow disruption for any given number of islands, while ensuring that each island contains only coherent generators was previously proposed and tested using IEEE test systems. The proposed algorithm is based on an exact Mixed Integer Linear Programming Formulation (MILP). However, since voltage instability has been found to be one of the main causes of several recent blackouts in the world, in this paper, the aforementioned algorithm is extended to consider voltage stability constraints. The extended ICI algorithm guarantees sufficient generation capacity (active and reactive power) to match the load consumption within each island. At the same time, it reduces the possibility of voltage collapse by assigning the weakest buses to the islands in such a way to be as close as possible to the sources or sinks of reactive power. The new constraints are expected to further improve the transient stability of the formed islands.

articleTitle: Methodology for preparing basis in modeling long-term energy consumption in households
publicationTitle: Mediterranean Conference on Power Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Energy Conversion (MEDPOWER 2018)
